[package]

version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2021"
rust-version = "1.58"
description = "Small, dependency-free integer arithmetic helpers with checked variants."
license = "MIT OR Apache-2.0"
readme = "README.md"
keywords = ["integer", "arithmetic", "checked", "no-std"]
categories = ["mathematics", "no-std"]

[dependencies]

[dev-dependencies]

# target_lib

Small, dependency-free integer arithmetic helpers with checked variants.

## Why

`a + b` is the obvious way to add two integers, but it panics on overflow in
debug builds and silently wraps in release builds. That difference is a classic
source of "works on my machine" bugs. This crate makes the trade-off explicit:
pick the panicking version, or pick the one that hands you back `None`.

## Usage

```toml
[dependencies]
target_lib = "0.1"
```

```rust
assert_eq!(target_lib::add(2, 3), 5);
assert_eq!(target_lib::checked_add(2, 3), Some(5));

// Overflow is reported, not wrapped.
assert_eq!(target_lib::checked_add(i32::MAX, 1), None);
```

## Behaviour

| Function | On overflow (debug) | On overflow (release) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `add` | panics | wraps |
| `checked_add` | returns `None` | returns `None` |

The crate is `no_std`, allocates nothing, and contains no `unsafe`.

## Development

```sh
cargo fmt --all --check
cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo test
cargo test --release   # exercises the release overflow behaviour
```

## MSRV

Rust 1.58.

name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main, master]
  pull_request:

env:
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        rust: [stable, beta]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@master
        with:
          toolchain: ${{ matrix.rust }}
          components: rustfmt, clippy

      - name: Format
        run: cargo fmt --all --check

      - name: Clippy
        run: cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings

      - name: Test (debug)
        run: cargo test --all-targets

      # Release builds drop debug assertions, so the overflow behaviour differs.
      - name: Test (release)
        run: cargo test --release --all-targets

      - name: Docs
        run: RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --no-deps
